Associate of Science in Intelligence Operations

bullets.text: Led a distributed team of 15 analysts in producing and disseminating 60+ weekly pages of threat intelligence reporting for Fortune 500, government, and nonprofit clients.
Integrated knowledge management tools and generative AI to cut report drafting time by ~80%, effectively 4–5x-ing team capacity while maintaining analytical rigor.
Conducted and oversaw 100+ annual risk assessments, escalating approximately two dozen high-risk cases each year to law enforcement or corporate security teams.
Designed and governed a cross-platform knowledge ecosystem (Jira, Google Workspace, Slack, Grammarly), including editorial standards, SOPs, and a 200-term glossary supporting cross-functional teams.

Partnered with Product, Engineering, Investigations, and Sales to align editorial and KM strategy with emerging capabilities, authoring the company’s first client-facing SaaS user guides and training materials.
Investigated emerging threats from influence operations, extremist movements, and online polarization to mitigate reputational and physical risks for high-profile clients.
Organized intelligence on thousands of tracked entities using Meltwater and proprietary tools, identifying collection gaps and directing alternative-platform scraping efforts.
Coordinated crisis management and threat-response operations with client communications, legal, and security teams, as well as outside investigators and law enforcement.
Designed and launched a HIPAA-compliant knowledge management system for 300+ employees and 50+ client representatives, enabling secure, role-based access to 400+ knowledge artifacts.
Led the migration from a legacy knowledge base to KMS Lighthouse, overseeing vendor evaluation, stakeholder alignment, and change management to improve operational efficiency.
Applied Topsight 2.0 research and workflow analysis methods to identify knowledge gaps, improve process clarity, and enhance information flow across operations, compliance, and IT.
Defined taxonomy, metadata, and publication standards for the KM ecosystem, auditing and maintaining articles for accuracy, consistency, and regulatory alignment.
Provided technical writing, copyediting, and content development services for Microsoft, nonprofits, and veteran support organizations.
Maintained a top-rated Upwork profile while completing a full undergraduate course load.
Fused HUMINT, SIGINT, and OSINT reporting to identify and mitigate terrorism, espionage, and insider-threat risks targeting NATO personnel and installations.
Reviewed 1,200+ base visitors annually to identify persons of interest, conducting follow-up investigations and issuing risk assessments for 19 field offices.
Designed and maintained a SharePoint- and Microsoft Forms–based RFI system, replacing a legacy email workflow with a searchable, trackable knowledge portal.
Conducted security and travel assessments for senior leaders, synthesizing classified intelligence, advisories, and geographic data to inform risk mitigation.
Represented U.S. interests at NATO Intelligence Fusion Center conferences, strengthening intelligence-sharing relationships with allied agencies.
Managed classification, versioning, and lifecycle control for sensitive intelligence products aligned to U.S., NATO, and host-nation standards.

bullets.text: Co-authored an intelligence production SOP adopted Corps-wide, improving consistency, timeliness, and analytic rigor across III Corps and subordinate units.
Deployed to Kabul as a dual-hatted Targeting Intelligence Sergeant and Knowledge Manager, maintaining a theater-wide targeting database and SharePoint portal.
Led an international training program that strengthened interoperability and analytic skills among coalition partners.
Led and mentored two intelligence teams in producing time-sensitive intelligence briefings, reports, and read books for senior commanders.
Used IBM i2 Analyst’s Notebook, DCGS-A, ArcGIS, and CPOF to perform link analysis, geospatial visualization, and threat tracking.
